strings.companies.integrations.syslog.hint: Live-mirrors this company's own honeypot alerts (real OpenCanary events only — never the internal/operational noise the Activity tab already filters out) to an external syslog server, as JSON, the moment each one arrives. Separate from the global syslog target on Settings → Integrations, which only ever carries audit log entries and never a honeypot alert — this is how a multi-tenant deployment routes each company's own alert traffic to that company's own SIEM instead of one shared target for the whole fleet. Best-effort: a delivery failure here is only ever logged, never blocks event ingestion. The database row (the Activity tab, GET /api/v1/events) is always the real record; this is just a live copy sent elsewhere.

strings.partials.updates.waiting_for_output: Waiting for output — this refreshes automatically.

strings.settings.general.background_checks.canar: reads whatever's new in OpenCanary's own log over SSH — powers the Activity tab and the Dashboard's activity-by-type section, no forwarder needed
strings.settings.general.background_checks.daily: purges old events/audit-log entries/monitoring samples/update runs past their retention, and rolls yesterday's per-company counts into the Dashboard trend chart
strings.settings.general.background_checks.facts: OS/kernel/CPU/RAM/disks, installed packages, and available updates
strings.settings.general.background_checks.hint: Every sweep below only runs for a honeypot with a confirmed host key fingerprint, and only fires on this cadence if Celery Beat is running (the `beat` service) — see Architecture in the wiki for the full list of what's scheduled.
strings.settings.general.background_checks.monit: CPU/load/RAM/network/disk-I/O and a failed-systemd-service count — the Monitoring tab's trend charts
strings.settings.general.background_checks.reach: TCP connect to the SSH port, no authentication
strings.settings.general.background_checks.sched: checks every enabled schedule's cron expression and fires whichever are due — cron itself is minute-grained, so this cadence isn't configurable
strings.settings.general.ssh_identity.heading: App SSH identity
strings.settings.general.ssh_identity.hint1: Honeypot Shelf connects to honeypots using this one shared key when "SSH key" is chosen as the authentication method — there's no key upload/generation to do per honeypot. To let it manage a honeypot, append the public key below to that honeypot's
strings.settings.general.ssh_identity.hint2: for the user Honeypot Shelf will connect as. Adding it to an already-managed honeypot can be done for you — see "Push pending key to all honeypots" below once you've generated a replacement key.
strings.settings.general.ssh_identity.pending_hi: A replacement key was generated {when} and is not active yet. Append it to every managed honeypot's

too (alongside the current one, don't remove the old line yet) before activating — activating switches which key Honeypot Shelf uses immediately, and any honeypot that hasn't got the new line yet will become unreachable.
strings.settings.general.ssh_identity.push_butto: Push pending key to all honeypots
strings.settings.general.ssh_identity.push_expla: "Push pending key to all honeypots" runs a command over SSH (using each honeypot's currently active key) to append the pending key above to

— for every honeypot using "SSH key" authentication with a pinned host key. It does not remove the old line or activate anything; it only saves you the manual copy-paste step above. Honeypots using password authentication aren't affected, since they don't use this key at all.
strings.settings.general.ssh_identity.push_resul: See the errors above for the rest.
strings.settings.index.heading: Settings
strings.settings.integrations.ldap.heading: LDAP login
strings.settings.integrations.ldap.hint1: When enabled, a user set to login method "ldap" (see
strings.settings.integrations.ldap.hint2: ) logs in with the same username/password form as a local account — the username is looked up in the directory below, and their password is checked against it, not against anything stored here.
strings.settings.integrations.ldap.tls_verify_hi: Only for "ldaps://" or StartTLS. Turn off only if you know this directory's certificate is self-signed or otherwise won't validate and you still want to use it — with it off, any certificate is accepted, with no protection against a honeypot-in-the-middle.
strings.settings.integrations.ldap.use_starttls: Use StartTLS (only relevant for a plain "ldap://" server URI)
strings.settings.integrations.leave_blank_unchan: Leave blank to keep the current value unchanged.
strings.settings.integrations.oidc.heading: OIDC login
strings.settings.integrations.oidc.hint1: When enabled, the login page shows a "Log in with OIDC" button. A user set to login method "oidc" (see
strings.settings.integrations.oidc.hint2: ) is matched by comparing their username against the claim named below in the ID token the provider returns — nothing is auto-created from this.
strings.settings.integrations.oidc.issuer_url_hi: (standard for any OIDC provider — Keycloak, Authentik, Entra ID, Okta, Google, ...).
strings.settings.integrations.oidc.provider_name: Shown on the login button ("Log in with {name}") instead of the generic "Log in with OIDC" — purely cosmetic.
strings.settings.integrations.smtp.heading: SMTP (email notifications)
strings.settings.integrations.smtp.hint: Configures the outbound mail relay used to send Notifications emails (My account → Notifications) — see Settings → Notifications for the shared email wording.
strings.settings.integrations.syslog.heading: Syslog forwarding
strings.settings.integrations.syslog.hint: Live-mirrors every audit log entry (every human-initiated mutation across the whole app) to an external syslog server (e.g. a SIEM) as it's written — RFC 5424 formatted, JSON message body, best-effort: a delivery failure here is only ever logged, never blocks the action being audited. Never carries honeypot alerts (OpenCanary events) — those have their own, separate, per-company target instead, on each Company's own Integrations tab. The database entry (exportable on the Security tab) is always the real record; this is just a copy sent elsewhere.
strings.settings.netbird.confirm_disconnect: Disconnect from NetBird? Honeypots reachable only over NetBird will become unreachable.
strings.settings.netbird.confirm_restart: Restart the NetBird connection? Honeypots reachable only over NetBird will be briefly unreachable.
strings.settings.netbird.heading: NetBird
strings.settings.netbird.hint: Connects Honeypot Shelf's own management-plane containers (web/worker) to your NetBird network, so a honeypot that's only reachable over NetBird (e.g. behind a NAT with no forwarded SSH port) still works with everything else in this app — the terminal, facts, updates, power, scheduling. This is separate from the NetBird setup key on the Initialize form, which joins the honeypot itself, not Honeypot Shelf. Requires the optional docker-compose.vpn.yml overlay to be applied — without it this tab can save your settings, but connecting will fail.
strings.settings.netbird.management_url_hint: Leave blank for NetBird Cloud (the public management service) — only set this for a self-hosted management server.
strings.settings.netbird.setup_key_hint: Stored encrypted. A NetBird setup key is single-use on NetBird's own side — this one connects Honeypot Shelf itself, not a honeypot.
strings.settings.netbird.setup_key_placeholder_s: Leave empty to keep the current key and just reconnect
strings.settings.netbird.setup_key_placeholder_u: Get one from your NetBird management console
strings.settings.security.audit_log.export_hint1: Every entry can also be exported for archival/compliance outside the app:
strings.settings.security.audit_log.export_hint3: page's own export links respect whatever search/outcome filter is set there).
strings.settings.security.audit_log.heading: Audit log
strings.settings.security.audit_log.hint1: Every entry is hash-chained (each links to the previous one's hash), so altering or removing an entry breaks the chain from that point on — see
strings.settings.security.audit_log.hint2: and the wiki page "Architecture" for how that works and what it doesn't protect against.
strings.settings.security.audit_log.retention_hi: Leave empty to keep every entry forever (the default). Otherwise, entries older than this are permanently deleted once a day — the chain's most recent entries and its ability to verify what remains are unaffected, since only the oldest end is ever pruned.
strings.settings.security.dashboard_trends.hint1: A background job records one daily snapshot of fleet-wide counts (online/offline honeypots, pending updates, ...) for the trend chart(s) on the
strings.settings.security.dashboard_trends.hint2: . This only controls how long those snapshots are kept — it doesn't affect the live counts themselves.
strings.settings.security.dashboard_trends.reten: Leave empty to keep every snapshot forever. Defaults to 90 days.
strings.settings.security.monitoring_history.hin: A CPU/RAM/disk-usage sample is stored for every honeypot on the Monitoring tab's own cadence (
, 2 minutes by default) — this only controls how long those samples are kept, not how often they're taken. A single honeypot can override this instance-wide default on its own Settings tab.
strings.settings.security.monitoring_history.ret: Leave empty to keep every sample forever. Defaults to 90 days.
strings.settings.security.notification_history.h: Every Notifications send attempt (real or test) is logged to the
page — this only controls how long that log is kept.
strings.settings.security.notification_history.r: Leave empty to keep every entry forever. Defaults to 90 days.
strings.settings.security.update_history.heading: Update run history
strings.settings.security.update_history.hint1: Each entry on a honeypot's Updates tab (the apt/flatpak/snap output from one run) is stored in full — this only controls how long those stored runs are kept, not whether updates themselves run. On a large fleet with recurring scheduled updates (see
strings.settings.security.update_history.hint2: ) this table can otherwise grow without bound. The fact that an update was triggered stays in the
strings.settings.security.update_history.hint3: regardless of this setting — only the stored run record/output is purged.
strings.settings.security.update_history.retenti: Leave empty to keep every run forever. Defaults to 90 days.
strings.settings.vpn.heading: VPN
strings.settings.vpn.hint: Connects Honeypot Shelf's own management-plane containers (web/worker) to a honeypot that's only reachable over a VPN — e.g. behind a NAT with no forwarded SSH port. Two mutually exclusive options below: NetBird or WireGuard. Connecting one automatically disconnects the other. Requires the optional docker-compose.vpn.yml overlay to be applied — without it, either section can save your settings, but connecting will fail.
strings.settings.wireguard.config_hint: Stored encrypted. Brought up verbatim via wg-quick — nothing here parses or modifies it.
strings.settings.wireguard.config_placeholder_se: Leave empty to keep the current config and just reconnect
strings.settings.wireguard.confirm_disconnect: Disconnect WireGuard? Honeypots reachable only over WireGuard will become unreachable.
strings.settings.wireguard.confirm_restart: Restart the WireGuard connection? Honeypots reachable only over WireGuard will be briefly unreachable.
strings.settings.wireguard.heading: WireGuard
strings.settings.wireguard.hint: Honeypot Shelf doesn't run its own WireGuard server — it joins an existing one you already run somewhere reachable, as a plain peer, the same as a honeypot does via its own Initialize option. Paste the peer config your WireGuard server admin (or its own UI) already gives out for any client — the same wg-quick .conf you'd use anywhere else.
strings.settings.wireguard.log_hint: Plain wireguard-tools keeps no log of its own — this is the control server's own record of connect/disconnect attempts and their results.

strings.users.new.auth_provider_hint: "local": a password set below. "ldap"/"oidc": leave the password field empty — the username is matched against the directory/provider instead (see Settings).
strings.users.new.password_hint: At least 12 characters. Required for "local" accounts, left blank otherwise. The user must change it on first login.
strings.users.new.scope_hint: A non-superadmin user always belongs to exactly one company, with either read-only or read + write access to its honeypots — nothing in between, and nothing shared across companies. The audit log and Settings are never available to a non-superadmin.
strings.users.new.title: Add user
strings.users.new.username_hint: Lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'. This is also the LDAP username and the OIDC identity, if used.
strings.settings.checks.background_checks.hint: How often each sweep runs, how long an SSH connection/update run may take, and how many honeypots the reachability sweep checks at once. Every sweep only runs for a honeypot with a confirmed host key fingerprint, and only fires on its cadence if Celery Beat is running (the `beat` service) — see Architecture in the wiki for the full list of what's scheduled.
strings.settings.checks.background_checks.ssh_co: How long a single SSH connection attempt is given before giving up. Takes effect on the very next check — no restart needed.
strings.settings.checks.background_checks.update: Max wall-clock time given to one full apt/flatpak/snap update run. Takes effect on the very next run — no restart needed.
strings.settings.checks.background_checks.reacha: How often the "is it alive" status badge's reachability sweep (a plain TCP connect, no authentication) runs for every honeypot. Takes effect the next time the `beat` service restarts.
How many honeypots the reachability sweep checks at once. Takes effect on the very next sweep — no restart needed.
strings.settings.checks.background_checks.facts_: How often OS/kernel/CPU/RAM/disk facts, installed packages, services, readiness, and available updates are refreshed for every honeypot. Takes effect the next time the `beat` service restarts.
strings.settings.checks.background_checks.monito: How often the Monitoring tab's CPU/RAM/disk-usage sample is taken for every honeypot (overridable per honeypot). Takes effect the next time the `beat` service restarts.
strings.settings.checks.background_checks.openca: How often this app connects over SSH and reads whatever's new in OpenCanary's own log for every honeypot (overridable per honeypot). Takes effect the next time the `beat` service restarts.
strings.settings.checks.background_checks.restar: The two timeouts and the concurrency cap above take effect immediately. The four interval settings only take effect the next time the `worker`/`beat` services restart — same as when they were configured in `.env`.
strings.settings.security.audit_log.retention_mo: Retention for these entries is configured under
strings.settings.security.monitoring_history.hin: A CPU/RAM/disk-usage sample is stored for every honeypot on the Monitoring tab's own cadence (configurable above, in Background checks) — this only controls how long those samples are kept, not how often they're taken. A single honeypot can override this instance-wide default on its own Settings tab.
strings.impersonation.banner_title: You are impersonating this account, signed in as {admin}
strings.users.impersonate.confirm: Sign in as "{name}"? Everything you do will be logged under their account.
strings.account.profile.email_hint: Used as the default destination for Notifications, unless you set a different address there. Not used for login.
strings.account.notifications.heading: Notifications
strings.account.notifications.hint: Get an email when a honeypot you can see logs a new alert, or when it becomes unreachable.
strings.notifications.title: Notifications
strings.notifications.email.heading: Notification email
strings.notifications.email.hint: By default, notifications go to your account email ({email}).
strings.notifications.email.label: Send notifications to a different address
strings.notifications.email.override_hint: Leave blank to use your account email above instead — e.g. for a shared team alias.
strings.notifications.subscriptions.heading: Honeypot subscriptions
strings.notifications.subscriptions.hint: Pick which honeypots you want to hear about, and how. Only honeypots you already have access to are listed.
strings.notifications.subscriptions.no_email_war: You don't have a notification email set yet — set one above, or these subscriptions won't have anywhere to send to.
strings.notifications.subscriptions.none_visible: You don't have access to any honeypots yet.
strings.notifications.subscriptions.alert_aria: Email me on new alerts from {name}
strings.notifications.subscriptions.minutes_hint: "After" is how long a honeypot must be continuously unreachable before you're emailed — set it per honeypot, e.g. shorter for something critical, longer for a flaky connection you don't want to hear about every time it blips.
strings.notifications.subscriptions.webhook_hint: "Send via" lets a subscription POST a plain JSON payload to a webhook URL instead of emailing — the URL must be a public http(s) address; a private/internal one is refused.
strings.notifications.history.title: Notification history
strings.notifications.history.hint: Your own last 200 notification send attempts — real and test.
strings.notifications.history.none: No notifications have been sent yet.
strings.settings.notifications.heading: Notification email templates
strings.settings.notifications.hint: The shared wording used for every Notifications email sent by this instance — see "Checks & retention" for background-check settings, and each user's own My account → Notifications for who actually receives one and for which honeypot.
strings.settings.notifications.self_service_hint: Who subscribes to what is self-service, per user — see

strings.settings.notifications.recovered.heading: Honeypot reachable again
strings.settings.notifications.blank_resets_hint: Leave a field blank to use the built-in default shown as its placeholder.
